title: The 10 Best Impact Driver Bit Sets
subtitle: Impact-rated screwdriver bit sets for cordless impact drivers, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: An impact driver hits a screw with short bursts of torque that snap ordinary bits at the tip. Impact-rated bits are made to flex instead of break. We ranked 10 best-selling sets from DEWALT, Makita, Milwaukee, Wiha, CRAFTSMAN and value brands on rating, review volume and features: a named torsion zone, a magnetic bit holder, nut drivers, and drill bits in the same case.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: 232-Piece Ultimate Screwdriver Bit Set, Cr-V Impact Driver Bit Set Includes Security Bits, Nut Driver, Ratchet Wrench and Bits Holder
avoid.flag: Sold for impact drivers, spec says round shank
avoid.verdict: The title sells it as an impact driver bit set, but the listing's own spec table lists a round shank, and an impact driver's chuck only takes 1/4 inch hex. It also gives two different model numbers.
reasons: The spec table lists the shank style as 'round shank'. Impact drivers only accept 1/4 inch hex shanks, so either the spec is wrong or part of the set won't fit the tool it's sold for.
The bits are chrome vanadium steel, the alloy used for hand-screwdriver bits. The listing names no torsion zone or impact rating beyond the title.
The listing gives model number 84075 and manufacturer part number 94401, so you can't check the set against a maker's spec sheet.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need impact-rated bits for an impact driver?
buyers_guide.a: Yes, if you drive more than a few screws. An impact driver delivers torque in rapid hammer blows, and a standard bit's hard tip cracks under them. Impact-rated bits use tougher steel (S2 or similar) and usually a narrowed torsion zone that twists slightly to absorb each blow.

A thinner section of the bit's shaft between the tip and the hex. It flexes a little on each impact so the tip doesn't take the full shock. DEWALT calls it FlexTorq, Wiha MaxxTor, Makita Impact XPS. Bits without one still work but wear out faster under heavy use.
Phillips #2 (PH2) and square #2 for most people, since they drive deck, drywall and cabinet screws. A set with several PH2 bits, like the Amazon Basics 42-piece with ten, saves a trip to the store.

buyers_guide.q: Do impact bit sets work in a regular drill?
buyers_guide.a: Yes. Every set here uses a 1/4 inch hex shank, which fits a drill's three-jaw chuck as well as an impact driver's quick-release collet. The reverse is not true: round-shank bits won't lock into an impact driver.

buyers_guide.q: Is a 100-plus piece set worth it?
buyers_guide.a: Only if you need the variety. Big sets pad the count with odd sizes and small precision bits you may never use. If you mostly build decks or hang cabinets, a 35 to 60 piece set with good PH2 and square bits plus a magnetic holder covers the work.
